version.changelog: Initial release: emotion-aware music companion for Feishu chats

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims (generate mood-matching audio and post it), but there are several mismatches and missing declarations — notably an undeclared API key, missing docs, and transmission of user text to a third-party service — that warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (detect emotion → build prompt → call a music A.I. → send audio to Feishu) matches the description. However, the code and SKILL.md require a MINIMAX_API_KEY and reference a MiniMax Music API even though the manifest lists no required environment variables or tools; additionally TOOLS.md (where the SKILL.md says the API key is configured) is missing. The dependency on a third-party music API is coherent with purpose but should have been declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stay within the described purpose (emotion recognition → prompt construction → generate → send). But they instruct the agent to: 1) read an environment variable (MINIMAX_API_KEY) that the manifest did not declare, 2) send user text as prompts to an external A.I. service (user emotional content is transmitted off-host), and 3) optionally persist a local history file (memory/mood-music-log.json) containing emotion records. These actions are reasonable for the feature but raise privacy considerations and should be explicitly declared.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + one script) reduces risk, but the Python script depends on the 'requests' package and network access; those dependencies are not documented. The script POSTs to https://api.minimaxi.com and then GETs an audio URL the API returns — standard but means arbitrary remote data will be downloaded based on the API response.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code expects MINIMAX_API_KEY (sensitive) but the skill manifest declares no required env vars. The SKILL.md also references TOOLS.md for configuration that isn't present. The skill will send user messages/emotional content to a third-party service (MiniMax) — this is proportional to generating music but is sensitive and must be disclosed. There is no mention of Feishu credentials in the manifest, yet the instructions use a 'message' tool to post to Feishu; ensure the agent's messaging tool handles Feishu auth separately and that no other credentials are required by the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent/always-on execution and does not modify other skills or system settings. It optionally writes a local JSON log (memory/mood-music-log.json) which could accumulate sensitive emotion records — this is within scope but should be opt-in and access-limited.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will send user messages (the text you input or the conversation snippets used to infer mood) to a third-party music-generation API (api.minimaxi.com) using an API key (MINIMAX_API_KEY). The manifest did not declare that env var or document required Python packages (requests) or the missing TOOLS.md. Before installing: 1) verify and trust the MiniMax provider and consider scoping/revoking the API key if misused; 2) confirm how the agent's 'message' tool obtains Feishu credentials (the skill doesn't declare Feishu auth); 3) be aware user emotional content will leave your environment and an optional local log file may store sensitive mood history; 4) require the author to update the manifest to list MINIMAX_API_KEY and runtime dependencies, provide TOOLS.md, and explain privacy/consent and retention for the local log. If you cannot verify the MiniMax endpoint or the missing documentation, avoid installing or test in an isolated environment.
